verdict: Apple posted its best quarter ever: revenue rose 16% to a record $143.8B on an all-time-high $85.3B of iPhone sales, and profit reached $42.1B.

segments.name: iPhone
segments.note: Its best quarter ever, on unprecedented demand for the iPhone 17 lineup, with all-time records in every geographic segment.

segments.name: Mac
segments.note: Mac computers; sales dipped 7% YoY against a strong year-ago quarter.

segments.name: Wearables, Home and Accessories
segments.note: Apple Watch, AirPods, HomePod and accessories; down 2% YoY.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: The App Store, iCloud, Apple Music, Apple TV, Apple Pay and warranties — an all-time record, up 14% YoY, and Apple's highest-margin business.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing future products and software; up 32% YoY as Apple invests in AI and new devices.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling and admin costs, including Apple's stores; up 4% YoY.

otherDetail: Other income (expense), net was +$150M: interest and dividend income modestly exceeded interest expense and other items.
follow100Note: The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: iPhone's best quarter ever
takeaways.text: iPhone revenue hit $85.3B, up 23% — an all-time record, with records in every geographic segment. iPhone alone was 59% of everything Apple sold.

takeaways.title: Services set another all-time high
takeaways.text: Services reached $30.0B, up 14%, and it is Apple's most profitable money: delivering those services cost $7.0B, against $67.5B of cost on $113.7B of product sales. The installed base passed 2.5 billion active devices.

takeaways.title: Record cash funded big returns
takeaways.text: Operating cash flow was nearly $54B in the quarter, and Apple returned almost $32B to shareholders — $24.7B of buybacks plus dividends.
